beintro-desc:
The year was 2070. Tensions between two Asian powers, having reached a boiling point, spilled over all too quickly.

International powers had no time to react and, before anyone knew it, a new Dark Age engulfed the world. The Golden Days were over.

The brief but deadly Pakistani-Indian War left an incredible footprint across the continent. Millions perished from famine, millions more were displaced. Soon the rest of the world felt the cold grip of ash. Economies collapsed. The satellites fell. The spirit of all nations was shaken.

But the Great Mistake did not end there. The lifestyle of modern societies, the exponential consumption of goods, the inability of people to look beyond tomorrow led to an even worse situation. The oceans swallowed entire cities. Societies enclosed on themselves, fighting wars of survival. The Earth, so close to globalization, fell far. The scars of bygone eons became visible once again. Hard times led to the development of new currents of thought, philosophies were forged to deal with the Great Mistake, with new technologies, with new problems.

But soon this era too will end. Civilizations across the world are awakening, one last time, to finish what they started, to bring balance to the world or to seek a second chance...

Beyond Earth
poi001-desc:
Franco-Iberia stands as a testament to the resilience and adaptability of human civilization in the face of catastrophe. Born from the fractured remnants of the Old European Union, it is more than just a nation—it is a symbol of unity forged through adversity.

While Europe avoided the most immediate devastation of the Great Mistake, it was soon overwhelmed by the ripple effects of global upheaval. Massive waves of refugees fleeing the chaos in Asia reshaped the continent, straining resources and exposing deep divides within the Old Union. Disagreements over priorities—whether to address the humanitarian crisis or prepare for environmental threats—splintered the fragile alliance. In the end, these pressures proved insurmountable, and the union collapsed under the weight of its internal conflicts.
poi002-desc: Franco-Iberia’s territorial ambitions and strategic positioning make it the spiritual successor to the Old European Union, but its vision is bolder and its methods more direct. With its sweeping claims over the western and southern parts of the continent, Franco-Iberia aspires to establish itself as the unchallenged leader of Europe. Yet, internal tensions persist. Even decades after its inception, leaders within Franco-Iberia’s sprawling bureaucracy grapple with conflicting ideologies—from those advocating pan-European integration to hardliners intent on consolidating Franco-Iberia’s power at the expense of its neighbors.
poi003-desc: However, this economic hegemony does not go unchallenged. Emerging powers, emboldened by new technologies and alliances, are eager to undermine Franco-Iberia’s dominance. To the north, the North Sea Alliance—a coalition of Scandinavian nations—wields its growing influence over polar trade routes, siphoning off lucrative markets once reliant on Mediterranean access. To the east, the Eurasian Federation consolidates its economic and military might, posing an existential threat to Franco-Iberia’s ambitions. Even the Maghreb, long seen as a subordinate trading partner, is rising in prominence, driven by advancements in renewable energy and agricultural innovation, challenging Franco-Iberia’s control over southern trade corridors.
poi004-desc: As the year 2200 unfolds, Franco-Iberia’s path forward remains uncertain. Its leaders must navigate a complex web of internal strife and external competition while striving to maintain the delicate balance between its ambition and stability. Yet, if history is any guide, Franco-Iberia’s ability to adapt, innovate, and persevere will ensure that it remains a formidable force on the global stage for decades to come.
poi005-desc:
Born into immense wealth, Élodie's lineage traces back to the nobility and privileged elite of Old France, extending a millennium before the Great Mistake. Her family's prestige and influence stemmed not from peerage but from the vast fortune amassed over the prior two centuries through holdings in agriculture, food processing, pharmaceuticals, and textiles.

Élodie entered the world at Europe's foremost fertility and maternity clinic in Braga as the only child of her parents. Raised in opulence along the Côte d'Azur and Costa del Sol, she became a media darling during her teenage years, though not always in a favorable light. Critics labeled her an isolationist and a European elitist, a reputation bolstered by her famously sharp tongue and incisive wit.

A staunch advocate of Western cultural traditions, Élodie believed it was the duty of the educated European elite to guide the masses, ensuring the preservation of high culture. She viewed the independence and sustainability of the new Union as the best means to achieve this vision.
poi006-desc:
The Union is undergoing a profound cultural renaissance, a revival reminiscent of the Renaissance and Enlightenment eras it holds dear. This resurgence is not merely about preserving the great artistic achievements of the past but fostering a dynamic environment for new generations of creators to explore and innovate. Through the Programe Artistice National, the Union has launched ambitious initiatives to nurture emerging artists and authors, encouraging them to build on its rich traditions while exploring new horizons in art and thought.

From the quietest rural villages to the busiest urban centers, citizens are drawn to newly opened museums, theaters, and cinemas, celebrating both heritage and contemporary creativity. European works, enriched by cultural infusions from North Africa, have become a source of unifying pride. The Union's Directorate-General for Education and Culture actively promotes and exports this vibrant culture, spreading its influence across the globe through media and other channels.

In this flourishing environment, the Union's guiding ethos—trésors de l'esprit—remains clear: a person's true wealth lies in the knowledge and culture they carry and share, not in material accumulation. It is little wonder that, amid uncertainty and upheaval, many seek to join the Union, drawn by its stability and dedication to the arts.
poi007-desc: The Mediterranean Sea, transformed by climate change but still vital, is the lifeblood of Franco-Iberia’s economy. Now a vast inland ocean with expanded shorelines, it serves as a crucial artery for trade and commerce. The nation’s ports, fortified and modernized, are hubs of activity, channeling goods and resources to and from key trading partners such as the industrial powerhouse of Padania to the northeast, the revitalized city-states of Greece, and the resource-rich but politically fragmented Maghreb to the south. Franco-Iberia’s dominance over Mediterranean trade routes is a cornerstone of its wealth and influence, allowing it to maintain a level of prosperity that few other nations can rival in this new world order.
poi008-desc: Franco-Iberia is governed by the Union Senate, a cornerstone of its democratic system, which deliberates and votes on all national matters. Esteemed worldwide as a model of effective democracy, the Senate fosters stability and a deep sense of civic engagement among its citizens. Direct votes from the populace are seamlessly processed through advanced computing systems, enabling efficient and transparent elections that strengthen public trust in the Union's governance.
poi009-desc:
Al-Hakim is one of the most influential figures in the French political landscape. Born to an Algerian immigrant family in the now-flooded suburb of Saint-Ouen, North Paris, he grew up in the high-crime neighborhoods of the city. As a young man, he became involved in the criminal underworld. However, government initiatives aimed at reforming at-risk youth recognized Al-Hakim's potential and offered him opportunities to change his path.

Determined to rebuild his life, Al-Hakim immersed himself in economics, philosophy, and history. By the age of 23, he had written his first book, marking the beginning of a widely popular literary career. His success culminated in the release of the controversial yet best-selling Hakim Manifesto. The book, known for its sharp critique of 21st-century culture and lifestyles, blamed societal decline on a group he labeled the seres faux, while advocating for the empowerment of the seres vrais. Although historians dismissed the book as lacking scholarly rigor, its message resonated deeply with the people of Franco-Iberia.

Buoyed by widespread public support, Al-Hakim used his newfound wealth to establish the Partido Populaire, which quickly became the second most powerful political force in Franco-Iberia. His movement continues to attract a growing base of followers, driven by his promises of reform and social justice.

Ultimately, Al-Hakim envisions a future of complete social equality and comprehensive political restructuring, striving to ensure that the seres faux never regain influence over society.
